output.summary: A rhizome-forming perennial of uncertain native origin, it grows across the Middle East and northern Africa and was traditionally planted on graves in Muslim regions. It has a violet-scented rhizome and fragrant white flowers, sometimes flushed with pale blue or lavender.
output.edibilityNote: Its violet-scented rhizome is used in sweets, to mature Chianti wine and in gin, although most parts are poisonous if eaten.
